chapters.name: Learning on Screen
chapters.headline: Collections and publishing tools for a membership charity
chapters.teaser: Migrated broadcast collections onto one accessible platform and gave the marketing and content teams the WordPress tools to publish on their own.
chapters.highlight: Collection migration, WordPress development, custom templates and shortcodes, plugins, REST APIs, UI/UX
intro: Learning on Screen (the British Universities and Colleges Film and Video Council) is an educational charity working with around 200 member institutions across higher, further and school education. Its services include [Box of Broadcasts (BoB)](https://learningonscreen.ac.uk/ondemand/), an on-demand television and radio streaming service, and the Television and Radio Index for Learning and Teaching (TRILT), which indexes UK broadcast listings from more than 560 channels, from 1923 onwards.
I joined a small Agile development team and grew into a role that sat between development, marketing and content, UX, and the membership team who work with students, academics and researchers.

stories.title: Bringing the collections into one accessible home

situation.text: The organisation was going through a digital transformation after the British Universities Film & Video Council (BUFVC) rebranded as Learning on Screen in 2015, but many collections were still on the old BUFVC website. Because they sat on a separate domain, with a different look, navigation and login, users had to move between two websites, which broke their journey.

task.text: Move the collections to the new platform without losing data, and make them consistent and accessible for every user.

action.text: Migrated the broadcast collections and research databases listed below onto the new platform.
Rebuilt the search forms, record views and audio players to be responsive and WCAG-compliant.
Built WordPress REST API endpoints so the older application could share the main site's header, footer and menus.

Worked with the membership team on what students and researchers needed: built a feedback form, gathered the responses and helped the marketing team analyse the data to decide which website improvements to make.
Supported users with the technical issues they reported.
Tested layout options on the test site before release.

result.text: All the collections were migrated and brought together in one Collections and Databases hub on learningonscreen.ac.uk. Members gave positive feedback on the consistent navigation and the modernised platform.

stories.title: Building flexible publishing tools for marketing campaigns, academic and research content

situation.text: Learning on Screen needed a CMS that would let its marketing and content teams create, edit and publish their own pages, from marketing campaigns to academic content such as courses and research.

task.text: Fill the gaps in the platform and make sure colleagues could publish confidently once the new site launched.

action.text: Built reusable components editors could add to any page: hero, tiles, cards, accordion, tabs and video player.
Integrated Advanced Custom Fields, MailerLite sign-ups, Google Tag Manager and cookie consent.

Coordinated reviews of an external agency's redesign of the main website with the content strategist and marketing specialist through Jira, Teams and meetings, and handled the handover with our tech lead.
Trained marketing colleagues to publish content in WordPress: wrote guides, presented to the team, ran one-to-one sessions and followed up with drop-in help by Teams message and email.
Worked with the UX team to build prototypes in Figma and review the site map and information architecture.

result.text: The WordPress platform runs on a custom theme with a library of around 45 in-house shortcodes, from heroes, tiles and cards to accordions, tabs and video players, plus in-house plugins such as a lightweight SEO plugin. Editors can combine these into flexible pages without writing code, and the same platform supported the collections migration, with custom templates and the REST API endpoint that shares its menus with the collections application. The content strategist, Head of Marketing, marketing specialist and membership manager all used it to create and update content themselves, including the copyright courses, research, about and awards pages.

stories.title: Symba Marketing: building a new Wix website the team can run themselves

situation.text: Symba Marketing supports charities, CICs and social enterprises with marketing. It needed a website that explained its services clearly and brought in enquiries.

task.text: Build the site from scratch and hand over a site the team could manage themselves.

action.text: Planned the page structure and navigation with the client before building.
Built the site on Wix, with clear calls to action to book a free consultation.
Covered SEO, Core Web Vitals and accessibility.
Trained the Symba team after launch so they could update their own content.

result.text: A clear marketing website that helps visitors understand Symba's services and book a free consultation, and that the client runs and updates without developer help.

stories.title: Keeping a B2B marketing site running, and building its relaunch

situation.text: I Like Music licenses music to broadcasters, businesses and schools. Its WordPress marketing site was live and business-critical, and a relaunch was planned.

task.text: Manage and extend the live site, and design and build the relaunched marketing site.

action.text: Extended the site with custom templates and fields (Elementor, Gravity Forms, ACF), enquiry forms to email and LinkedIn tracking.
Agreed requirements for the relaunch with the client services team, then designed it in Figma and built it.
Organised the new homepage around the customer journey, so each type of customer can quickly see the service is for them and find a clear next step.

result.text: Plugin updates are now tested on staging before they go live, keeping the business-critical site stable. The relaunched homepage gives each type of customer a clear next step: start on the platform or talk to the sales team.

stories.title: Development work for the new platform

situation.text: I Like Music was migrating its infrastructure and relaunching its platform, covering client service management, a radio streaming service and catalogue ingestion.

task.text: Build features for the new platform and keep the catalogue data ingestion pipelines reliable.

action.text: Contributed to AWS Lambda consumers and database ingestion pipelines for catalogue data.
Maintained and ran ingestion for commercial and production music catalogues.
Wrote Python tools to validate catalogues before they were loaded.
Developed client portal features as part of the move from the legacy app.
Produced usage reports with Python, SQL and Excel.

result.text: Commercial and production catalogues continued to be loaded and checked throughout the migration, clients had the portal features they needed for the move, and the business had usage reports to work from.

lessons.title: Every break in the journey costs users
lessons.text: Moving the collections showed me that a separate domain, login and menu is enough to lose people. Consistency across platforms matters as much as any single page.

lessons.title: Test before it goes live
lessons.text: A plugin update that needed a newer PHP version took a business-critical site offline. Now every update is checked on staging first.

lessons.title: Tools only help if people can use them
lessons.text: Building components was half the job. Guides, a team presentation, one-to-ones and follow-up help are what got colleagues publishing on their own.

lessons.title: Turn feedback into improvements
lessons.text: Feedback forms and analytics gave the team evidence for what to improve next, instead of guesses.
